declared_purpose: Answer Garmin health, recovery, workout, time and route questions using health metrics and activity files; generate interactive HTML charts and framework-based insights for Clawdbot. JSON output and analysis workflows are explicit requirements. The referenced MCP server is a separate package. Sources: SKILL.md:1-19,110-180,218-231; references/mcp_setup.md:1-16,42-62.

data_operations.operation: Install dependencies and optionally create a configuration template
data_operations.data_scope: Dependency identifiers garminconnect, fitparse and gpxpy; example credential fields containing placeholders.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: pip and its configured package sources if retrieval is needed; skill-local config.json.
data_operations.condition: Installation runs; alternative pip commands follow failures. The template is copied only when config.json is absent.

data_operations.operation: Read login credentials locally; document optional credential persistence
data_operations.data_scope: Account email and password from CLI arguments, config.json or GARMIN_EMAIL/GARMIN_PASSWORD.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authentication process memory; documented file options retain credentials in config.json or ~/.clawdbot/clawdbot.json.
data_operations.condition: Login uses per-field fallback: CLI, local configuration, then environment. The helper does not directly read clawdbot.json; host environment injection is unresolved.

data_operations.data_scope: Account email and password; authentication exchange managed by the dependency.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Garmin Connect through garminconnect/garth; exact hosts and wire payloads are not supplied.
data_operations.condition: The login command has both credential fields. Authentication is necessary for private account access; dependency internals remain unresolved.
Successful initial login. Directory permissions are changed to 0700 after token writing and the connection test; individual token files and serialization are dependency-controlled.

data_operations.operation: Restore sessions and fetch daily summaries for validation
data_operations.data_scope: Saved tokens; today's user-summary response, including any daily statistics and identity fields returned.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tokenstore and authentication-process memory; authenticated summary requests go to Garmin through the library.
data_operations.condition: Login tests the connection once. get_client restores tokens and fetches a summary before remote commands. Successful status additionally fetches another summary. Local activity parse/query/analyze branches do not call get_client.

data_operations.data_scope: Login email, returned displayName, tokenstore paths and exception text.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: stderr and its caller; downstream logging or remote delivery is unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Email is printed during login; displayName during successful login/status tests; errors and paths are printed on their corresponding branches.

data_operations.operation: Fetch selected core metrics and return projected fields
data_operations.data_scope: Sleep stages and related measurements; HRV summaries/baselines/status; Body Battery charging and extrema; heart-rate summaries; activity names/types and performance fields; stress levels/durations.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Garmin receives authenticated date-based requests; responses enter Python memory and selected fields return through stdout to the caller.
data_operations.condition: The selected metric determines fetching. Both explicit dates override defaults; otherwise positive --days N produces daily loops from today minus N through today, inclusive. No health-data file write is implemented here.

data_operations.operation: Fetch and return account profile identifiers
data_operations.data_scope: Full name, display_name and email, when returned.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Garmin library responses enter process memory; projected identifiers return through stdout to the caller.
data_operations.condition: The profile metric is explicitly selected; ordinary metric commands do not call fetch_profile.

data_operations.operation: Compute a combined summary and return its underlying records
data_operations.data_scope: Sleep, HRV, Body Battery, heart rate and activities; derived averages, activity count and calorie total. Stress is not fetched by this function.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local computation; summary and all five projected record arrays return to the caller through stdout.
data_operations.condition: summary is selected, including the entry document's sleep-question recipe and general analysis workflow.

data_operations.operation: Fetch one extended metric and pass through its response
data_operations.data_scope: Selected training, body composition, weight, oxygen, respiration, movement, hydration, stress, fitness or intraday heart-rate response. Returned objects are not field-projected.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Garmin through the dependency; complete selected response in process memory and stdout to the caller.
data_operations.condition: One metric is selected. Dated metrics default to today; weight history defaults to a range beginning 30 days earlier. Exact response fields are unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Read daily time-series data and select a nearby measurement locally
data_operations.data_scope: A day's selected heart-rate, stress, Body Battery or steps response; requested time/date and selected value, with actual time also returned for heart rate.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Garmin receives a date-based metric request; nearest-point selection occurs locally and its result returns through stdout.
data_operations.condition: A time query is selected and response formatting permits a match. The code does not send a narrower time window or persist the series.

data_operations.operation: Download and persist an activity export
data_operations.data_scope: Selected activity ID and complete original/FIT, GPX or TCX response bytes; potentially route and physiological/performance data.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Garmin receives the authenticated activity/format request; bytes are written to output_dir/activity_<activity_id>.<format>, defaulting to /tmp.
data_operations.condition: download is selected with an activity ID and authentication succeeds. Persistent export is the requested outcome; no cleanup is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Read local activity files and return parsed, selected or aggregate data
data_operations.data_scope: All non-null FIT record/lap/session fields; GPX coordinates, elevation, time, speed, heart-rate field and bounds. Parse returns full extracted data; successful FIT queries return a whole matching record; analysis returns statistics.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local parser/process memory and stdout to the caller; these branches contain no Garmin request or file write.
data_operations.condition: parse, query or analyze is selected with a supported file and dependency. Query/analysis success depends on available record fields; GPX parsing does not provide the FIT-style records expected by analysis.

data_operations.operation: Project chart data, persist HTML and optionally open a browser
data_operations.data_scope: Selected sleep duration/score, Body Battery peaks, HRV/resting-HR series, activity-type counts/calories, averages/totals, dates and generation time; not complete API responses.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Explicit --output HTML file, or a system temporary HTML file with delete=False; default browser receives the temporary file URL.
data_operations.condition: Only selected chart categories are fetched; dashboard selects all four charts. --output writes without opening; the default path writes and automatically opens. No cleanup is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Load an external chart script into the health-data page
data_operations.data_scope: Fixed Chart.js resource request and browser connection/request metadata. Embedded chart data shares the execution context with the loaded script; no explicit health-data upload is shown.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: cdn.jsdelivr.net receives the resource request; externally supplied JavaScript executes locally in the browser page.
data_operations.condition: Generated HTML is opened and its external script is loaded. Actual CDN-script behavior, headers and subsequent requests are unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Infer health and recovery attributes under the documented analysis workflow
data_operations.data_scope: Derived assessments of recovery, fitness, stress, possible illness and overtraining from metric trends; recommendations and flags.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Analyzing agent and its user/caller; provider routing or additional persistence is not specified.
data_operations.condition: The user requests insights and the agent applies the prescribed framework. These are conditional interpretations, not additional sensor measurements or automatic script outputs.

data_operations.data_scope: Fetched historical health data and newly fetched dates.
data_operations.condition: A user or agent adopts the caching recommendations. No cache implementation, location, retention limit or deletion procedure is supplied.

data_operations.operation: Describe manual token deletion using a mismatched path
data_operations.source: Entry privacy note versus authentication implementation
data_operations.data_scope: Documented token file ~/.clawdbot/garmin-tokens.json; implemented tokenstore is ~/.clawdbot/garmin.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local filesystem only; no supplied remote revocation operation.
data_operations.condition: A user follows the deletion advice. The referenced file differs from the helper's actual directory, so removal of current helper tokens is not established.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Extra authenticated requests to Garmin; summary responses in authentication-process memory.
potential_excess.condition: Every successful get_client path performs a summary probe; successful status performs another. Login also fetches a summary after authentication.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Authentication validation is necessary; unconditional daily-statistics fetching is an implementation choice. The second status fetch is explicitly redundant.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Detect invalid authentication and enable the requested operation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use the requested metric request to detect failure where practical; retain one status probe and avoid the duplicate summary fetch. Use a lighter probe only if supported.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve invalid-token handling and status verification; upstream support for lighter probes is unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Account email and returned displayName in progress/status messages.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: stderr and any caller that captures it; further persistence is unknown.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Authentication feedback is useful; identifying the account in every diagnostic is additional data within that feedback.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Report success, failure and actionable authentication state.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit identity fields by default or expose them through an explicit account-identification option.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep requested profile results and any explicitly needed multi-account identification.

potential_excess.data_scope: HRV, Body Battery, heart rate and activities fetched alongside sleep; all five underlying arrays returned.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Additional Garmin metric requests and stdout to the caller.
potential_excess.condition: The entry's last-night sleep recipe invokes summary --days 1 solely to report sleep hours and score.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The broad command is explicitly prescribed by the entry document, although its stated answer requires only sleep. This reduction requires changing that recipe.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve and report the relevant night's sleep duration and score.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a sleep-only query for that question and return the required sleep fields. Preserve comprehensive summary for broad health analysis.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep additional metrics when the question asks about recovery or combined health; preserve correct night/date selection.

potential_excess.data_scope: One additional calendar day's metric request beyond N daily dates.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Garmin daily-query boundary; returned records may reach stdout or selected chart HTML.
potential_excess.condition: Positive --days N is intended to mean N daily dates: start is today minus N and daily loops include both endpoints, producing N+1 attempted dates.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry describes last-N-day queries; inclusive explicit date ranges can legitimately cover both endpoints.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve the requested period without adding an unintended day.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Define --days semantics and use today minus N-1 when N calendar dates are intended.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve explicit inclusive --start/--end ranges and any deliberately defined rolling-window behavior.

potential_excess.data_scope: All fields of a selected FIT record, including unrelated route or physiological fields when present.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Query result printed to stdout and returned to the caller; no remote disclosure is established.
potential_excess.condition: A narrow elevation, pace or heart-rate question is answered using the generic activity query.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A matching data point is required; returning every field is additional data within that required result. Full-record queries remain a supported use.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Locate the relevant point and provide the requested measurement with sufficient matching context.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Add field selection or project the result to requested measurements and necessary time/distance context.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain an explicit full-record mode and full parse/export behavior for comprehensive analysis.

potential_excess.data_scope: Browser resource-request metadata; embedded health chart data available to externally supplied page code.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: cdn.jsdelivr.net receives the resource request; its script executes in the local health-data page. Health-data transmission to the CDN is not shown.
potential_excess.condition: Generated chart HTML loads its external Chart.js dependency.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Interactive visualization is required; fetching its implementation from an external host is a replaceable implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Render the same interactive charts and tooltips.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Package Chart.js locally and reference the local asset.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the required chart functionality and version compatibility. Actual third-party script behavior remains unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Rendered health series, dates, derived statistics and generation time.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: System temporary HTML file created with delete=False.
potential_excess.condition: A chart is generated without --output; the file persists without an implemented cleanup step.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A browser-readable file is needed for automatic opening; indefinite retention after viewing is not specified as an outcome.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep the chart available while the user views it.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Provide a bounded cleanup lifecycle or session-based serving, with explicit saving for retention.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not remove the file before browser loading or required reloads; preserve explicit --output exports.

potential_excess.data_scope: Reusable session tokens left in the implemented tokenstore.
potential_excess.condition: A user follows the entry's advice to delete ~/.clawdbot/garmin-tokens.json, expecting to remove the helper's access.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry promises user-controlled access removal; its deletion target differs from the implemented persistence boundary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Remove the actual locally reusable session credentials when access removal is requested.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Correct the deletion instructions or supply a logout operation targeting TOKEN_DIR; separately explain remote revocation if supported.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Account for intentionally shared clients before deletion. Local deletion alone must not be represented as proven Garmin-side token invalidation.

unknowns: The packaged-source audit is complete. Missing garminconnect/garth internals block verification of exact Garmin hosts, authentication payloads, additional library requests, token serialization, automatic refresh and token-file retention (scripts/garmin_auth.py:14-19,47-51,84-88).

Exact response schemas and upstream field/time-window filtering are unresolved. Extended helpers return unprojected dependency responses, so their complete data scope and opportunities for upstream narrowing cannot be established (scripts/garmin_data_extended.py:15-198; scripts/garmin_query.py:82-206).

The CDN script body is absent. Its access to page data does not establish remote health-data transmission; subsequent requests, headers, cookies and referrer behavior remain unknown (scripts/garmin_chart.py:23-29,120-164).

Standalone MCP behavior is unresolved: only a redirect/setup document is packaged. Its claimed shared token-file paths differ from the Python helper's directory; authentication sharing, disclosure and persistence cannot be verified (references/mcp_setup.md:1-16,54-62; scripts/garmin_auth.py:21-22).

Clawdbot environment injection, automation, report delivery, model routing and caller retention are not supplied. Ordinary stdout/stderr returns do not establish further remote sharing (SKILL.md:37-57,143-143; references/mcp_setup.md:42-48).

Actual filesystem ownership, token-file modes, backups and browser caches are unknown. Directory chmod occurs after token dumping; it does not establish individual file permissions or cleanup elsewhere (scripts/garmin_auth.py:43-62; scripts/garmin_chart.py:544-556).
Optional cache storage, retention and deletion remain unspecified; package-source recipients used by pip also depend on unprovided configuration (references/api.md:229-233,296-302; install.sh:22-32).

No supplied operation establishes remote token revocation. Deleting a local file or directory cannot be assumed to invalidate sessions retained by Garmin or the separate MCP implementation (SKILL.md:249-254; references/mcp_setup.md:54-62).
